key_insight: BioMem introduces HMRU, a training-free memory framework reporting an average 8.6% relative improvement across biomedical question-answering and conversational memory benchmarks.
clinical_relevance: More reliable memory could help biomedical LLM agents use relevant prior information, but these results do not establish clinical safety or patient benefit.
method: Evaluated five memory approaches across four LLMs.
Tested biomedical reasoning, clinical prediction, and long-term conversational memory.
Developed HMRU to improve evidence accessibility and task-aware use.
evidence_signal: HMRU reduced conversational answer errors by 24.9% and closed 48.0% of the performance gap to full-context inference, with additional gains in selected clinical prediction tasks.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify dataset sizes or clinical deployment validation; retrieval relevance and information fidelity remain important implementation concerns.
paper_title: BioMem: Agentic Memory for Biomedical LLM Agents
